We keep it on a side table in the loving room and just grab it once or twice a day to get in a few minutes. We both already feel a difference.

I have worked all positions and found them to be very effective. The older version had a plastic liner on the finger holder. That made it very easy to put the whistle in your mouth and pull your fingers out. That way you can use both hands and arms to give signals while holding the whistle with your teeth. I'm sure I'll figure out a way to get my fingers out of the holder when needed, but I think I prefer the plastic versus the rubber.

text_fidelity_a:
Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper This is made of a light, soft, flame retardant flannel.

It has a long white zipper which goes almost to the toes, with an easy snap at the top.

The fabric is cute with Patriots logo.

It has white stitching for accent.

It is 100% polyester. I prefer cotton which breathes better.

It has two pesky labels at the top back.

You are supposed to turn this inside out when you wash on cold, gentle cycle with like colors. Do not use fabric softener or it will impact flame retardant ability. Non-chlorine bleach. Tumble dry low.

It was made in Bangladesh.

Suggestions for improvement: use more cotton in fabric, substitute print for labels at upper back, and perhaps skip the flame retardant chemicals. 3.5 stars

Here's some info which discourages flame retardant fabrics close to children's skin:
A study published in August 2014 found that PBDEs (polybrominated diphenyl ethers), the most commonly used fire-retardant chemicals, were linked to numerous health problems.

Researchers found the chemicals were to blame for:

thyroid disruption
early onset of puberty
cognitive problems
delayed mental and physical development
“The chemicals used to make pajamas and other consumer products flame-retardant show up in water, wildlife, and human breast milk,” says pediatrician Michael Macknin, MD.

According to Dr. Macknin, the chemicals in fire retardants do diminish the flammability of products treated with them and have been associated with decreased burn injuries in children. However, the chemicals aren’t well-bound to the fabric fibers at times and can leech out. This allows the fire-retardant chemicals to float free in the environment.

“The long-term impact these chemicals may have on health and cognition is not closely scrutinized,” says Dr. Macknin. “They are often put on the market without long-term studies of their safety.”

Other dangers besides pajamas
These chemicals are found in furniture and mattresses as well as cell phones, television remotes and numerous other consumer plastics, says Dr. Macknin.

“If the tag on a sofa or mattress you’re planning to buy says, ‘this article complies with flammability requirements of California Bureau of Home Furnishings Technical Bulletin 117’, or language to that effect, it likely contains pounds of PBDEs,” he says.

You’ll find this sort of notice on numerous children’s products like car seats, strollers, toys and changing mats. According to Dr. Macknin and other health experts, these added chemicals may put your child at a greater risk than the flames they claim to inhibit. An alternative to chemically treated flame-retardant pajamas are close-fitting pajamas made of natural fibers. Some fabrics meet smolder standards without added chemicals.
text_fidelity_b: Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper

text_fidelity_a:
Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway This is a great way to store 12 sets of polyhedral dice for D&D and similar games. I'm not sure if you strictly-speaking need waterproof storage for that, but while the O-ring may be overkill, the locking clasps and overall durability are a cut above what you usually find on parts organizers. This is never, ever going to come open unexpectedly and spill its precious contents all over the place!

With the dividers installed as shown in my photo, 8 areas hold a set of 7 polyhedral dice perfectly. Five of those will also hold a set of 12 six-sided dice. The four larger areas hold somewhat more; I have 10 d20's in one of them comfortably.

The downside of this approach is that you're certainly not going to sneak up on anyone while carrying one of these full of plastic/resin dice. And if you're into metal dice, or the sort of gemstone dice where each of them costs more than this whole container, then this probably isn't how you want to store them. (But you could probably pad them properly with a bit more work.)

Color of the O-ring seems to vary. I have two black and one blue, but the Plano part number stamped into it is the same for all three.

If you are the sort of person who needs to compactly and securely transport a lot of dice, this is the best way I've found to do it.

KastKing SuperPower Braided Fishing Line - Abrasion Resistant Braided Lines – Incredible Superline – Zero Stretch – Smaller Diameter – A Must-Have! You get what you pay for with braided line. Ignore the LB ratings and pay more attention to Diameter vs Average Breaking Strain. I've found many of the lower priced braids will break at or below the "LB rating" - Where the premium braids break at a higher number than the "LB rating". Then you have to consider abrasion, slickness of the line, and how well the coatings and/or dyes stay on the line. If you are targeting smaller freshwater or panfish you might be ok with this line - If you are hitting bigger fish and using premium gear, personally would invest in a better braid and have confidence in your connection.

I've given up on finding a bargain braid and now just invest in premium braid lines and will never look back.

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite New York 1210 Bike Chain Lock, 3.25 Feet Long Heavy Duty Anti-Theft Sold Secure Gold Bicycle Chain Lock with Evolution Disc Lock and Keys for Ultimate Security E-Bike, Motorcycle, Scooter I own a chain just like this. See my review here: [[ASIN:B000AMVPUM Kryptonite New York Chain 3' With Key Lock]]

The problem with these giant chains is a sense of added security, but I'm not convinced you get it with something like this. Big bolt cutters will demolish this thing (for evidence, search youtube for "security chains vs. bolt choppers", skip to 6min24s... this chain gets demolished in less than a minute. Granted, they're huge bolt cutters. But someone running around in a van at 3AM isn't going to care.). Couple the questionable security with how big of a pain this thing is to lug around (I've owned the chain for years) and I can't imagine it's worth it.

Anyway, since no bike lock seems to be impervious to bike theft, it's important for people to realize the only true security is to store the bike within sight (your home, place of work, near you on a restaurant patio, etc.). I imagine the latest and greatest u-locks are a better option due to the shear time it takes to grind through them (with bolt cutters not being an option), but I'd wager all bike chains are susceptible to big bolt cutters.
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite New York 1210 Bike Chain Lock, 3.25 Feet Long Heavy Duty Anti-Theft Sold Secure Gold Bicycle Chain Lock with Evolution Disc Lock and Keys for Ultimate Security E-Bike, Motorcycle, Scooter

text_fidelity_a:
FDW Magnetic Bike Trainer Stand for Indoor Riding, Steel Bicycle Exercise Training Stand with Noise Reduction Wheel,Stationary Bike Resistance Trainer for Road & Mountain Bikes This stand is for bikes with NUTS not skewers and the plastic end caps are not necessary. I get better more secure mount without them.
This is a good stand for the money. The weather is wet and cold here and I used to hang my mountain bike up all winter. Here's what I have learned so far. The plastic caps that come on the axle mounts can shear right off if the axle does not protrude enough. One side of my axle stuck out a bit more than the other and the SHORT side was supporting all the weight on the plastic cap. It dropped off this morning and startled me a bit. I looked and saw the problem right away. I threw the mangled cap away and reset the axle after loosening the roller part. The metal to metal connection is much better and no harm comes to the bike nut or frame because only MILD torque is required to secure your bike axle. the weight is vertical, if you see the frame of the stand SPREAD at all you have over torqued! Just snug is fine. It's easy to move the tire to track in the middle of the roller, just loosen one side and then snug the other side till your tire is dead center. The roller tension is kind of by feel. If your tire is really inflated like mine you will need a bit of pressure to keep it from slipping, you can usually feel if the tire is slipping on the roller. Find a medium gear and stick with it, shifting gears is pointless and you'll run the roller to death on high gear anyway. The adjustment for roller resistance is a nice big knob that comes off and on with no tools. My street tires make almost no noise. If you are taking the bike off and on frequently. FIRST take the resistance knob off your handlebars and set it out of the way. SECOND take the roller pressure off so that it's free of the rear tire. THIRD remove the block riser from under the front tire or it will make it hard to get off the rear axle. FOURTH loosen the axle holders, it will help if another person can steady the bike while you do this but I did it by myself (this time). The riser block I got was a bit tall (3 inches) as a reviewer said the stand raised the rear wheel about 3 inches. That put me about 1/2 inch high in the front, but you don't want a lot of pressure on your hands anyway since you are stationary and not going anywhere. I found a short step stool helps me on and off the bike as it is now pretty high. Get on and off as carefully as you can. I will add more if needed to this review.
text_fidelity_b: FDW Magnetic Bike Trainer Stand for Indoor Riding, Steel Bicycle Exercise Training Stand with Noise Reduction Wheel,Stationary Bike Resistance Trainer for Road & Mountain Bikes

text_fidelity_a:
Exerpeutic Gold Heavy Duty Foldable Exercise Bike with 400 lbs Weight Capacity So like a good many people, being stuck at home with the parks closed, limited space, and etc, I looked into a bike to use during periods of extended stay at home.

I looked into many bikes on amazon within my budget, and this one (originally the previous version) was the one that caught my eye.

For build quality, if I were to rate this out of 5...it would get a 3. I say this because during the build, the quality of the parts didn’t feel like how all of the reviews made it seem to be. My father helped me out during the build, and commented and the bare minimum level quality of the tools you get and etc. That’s really what makes the build a minor issue. You would think that you could go firm when screwing things in, but trying to do that, it makes you feel like you’re going to break the bike piece! A comment my father made rings a bit true. “They don’t build these things to be put together by people who know parts or tools. They just dumb it down for people who have never touched a tool!” That’s my quick quip about the building process. Parts seem good. Your tools are bare minimum level quality and don’t go too firm or hard when screwing things in. It's sturdy, but I would not put all of your weight on one point of it. For example, don't lean all the way forward, or put all your weight to one particular side!

Using the bike, I would say things are a 3.5 or 4 out of 5. Look, you’re not going to get the same workout you would comparing this product to a bike you would use at the gym or one of those $500-$700 bikes. These bikes are more for being “active” versus training or working out. It’s better than doing nothing at all. If you think that you’re buying this bike to train or workout, it’s the wrong product for you! Resistance levels feel good, and gives a decent warmth to the muscles after some time. But I would not risk trying to do HIIT training too often on this bike. MAYBE 2-3 times a week at most. The seat cushion could be better. For something so wide or large, you're not actually using the whole seat when you're using the bike and prolonged use of the bike will cause discomfort below. Maybe you get used to it, or more cushion to where you personally need it most!

Overall, I would say this product is good for BEGINNERS or those who feel intimidation, shyness, or some kind of adverse feeling towards going to the gym or being out in public. Or, like in recent situations at the time of this review, you’re stuck at home! This bike is a “better than nothing” solution (one of many). This can definitely compliment a healthy diet and lifestyle, but don’t expect this to be the sole way to workout and lose weight. They say, abs are made in the kitchen and that’s 1000% true. Burn like 100-200+ calories using this bike and use that to compliment you eating less each day (250 to 500 calories a day less!) You will lose weight that way if you’re looking to lose weight.

I will revise this review if, over time, the parts break quickly or if there’s something that’s worth mentioning. Or if this gives some results after a good 2-3 months of use! For now, this product gets a decent 4/5, for those who are new to exercising (note I don't say working out and training). 3/5 for those who are used to the gym or are more experienced!
text_fidelity_b: Exerpeutic Gold Heavy Duty Foldable Exercise Bike with 400 lbs Weight Capacity

It really isn't very hard, but if you'd like more than a picture and a few half-sentences, you won't find it. The kit comes with everything you need, but includes zero extra pieces.

We installed 2/3 of this rack with no problem. The third segment continued to pull away from the wall no matter how we hung it. Looks like a few of the wall anchors failed, and ultimately, it needs to hold quite a bit of weight if you're using all three segments to capacity, so we felt safer putting up just two.

Fortunately, the other two segments hold all the bikes we need it to, and it holds them well. We fit four wide, although this is the kind of system that requires you to remove pretty much all of the bikes when you are trying to pull a specific bike. It works for our family if we hang them in an alternating pattern, and it feels very sturdy.

I don't know if this is a glowing recommendation or one that should be followed with caution, so three stars feels appropriate.

It's not because I'm playing it on a modern TV that upscales it badly - I play this on my HDTV with a RetroTink that makes the NES look like a million bux. It's just that the video output from this thing is really sorry. Play it on a CRT if you still have one - that will soften the flaws a little bit.

I'm very sad that the plug'n'play generation ended here because a version of this with HDMI out and Wii-style accelerometers to more accurately detect nudges would make for an amazing experience. I'm still giving this five stars because the tables are great and it feels great to play, and it costs as much as a frugal fast casual lunch. text_fidelity_a:
Oakley Flight Deck Ski Goggles, Large-Sized Fit I started my goggle search in the fall and was fairly convinced that I would go with a dedicated goggle company like Smith (my outgoing goggles) or Zeal with their automatic lens technology. I even bought some Zeal goggles but ended up not liking the lens or fit at all (none of their frames fit me and my Bern Rollins helmet well). I didn't really consider Oakley at first because they seem to be doing so many things outside of lens technology and innovation and had become a huge brand rather than the focused eyewear company of the 80s and 90s. The more I investigated this, the more I realized I was mistaken...

Prizm technology is the real deal and not just marketing fluff. I've been an avid skier for 33 years and these goggles are the best I've used when it comes to all-conditions contrast and overall visibility. Even the totch lens is good in overcast, snow/blowing snow conditions. The size of the lens and field of vision is also great with no visible distortion (another thing that I noticed with the Zeal). The anti-fog is not the greatest (in terms of initial fog resistance) but so far it seems to dissipate quickly when it does fog up. The only other complaint I would have is that the word "Prizm" in the lower left eye field of vision on the outside of the lens is a bit distracting. I wish it was smaller or not there at all. Neither of these things will drop a star from my rating but maybe a 1/2 star if I could. The point is that the pros far outweigh the cons and I'm a true believer in Prizm! Well done, Oakley. [...] This video on youtube gives a great in-depth look at what's behind Prizm.
text_fidelity_b: Oakley Flight Deck Ski Goggles, Large-Sized Fit

text_fidelity_a:
Sailnovo Electric Bike, Electric Bicycle with 18.5mph Electric Bikes for Adults Teens E Bike with Pedals, 14" Waterproof Folding Mini Bikes with Dual Disc Brakes [[VIDEOID:e7db44ebf2cc5b42c4a2213aa6e49919]] We really love our new electric bike. The set up was super easy and only required that we remove the packaging, insert the seat, unfold the handle bar, adjust the grip, and screw the pedals in. The recommended initial charge is 5 hours – ours took about 4 hours for the light to turn green.

The bike will provide assistance while pedaling or you can use the throttle on the handle bar to power the bike unassisted. I’m 145lbs and the bike cruises at 12-13mph on flat ground using just the throttle without pedaling. The battery display adjusts according to how hard the assist is working. Pedaling uphill will seemingly drop the remaining charge, but you “gain” it back when the elevation levels out. As far as we can tell, pedaling does not recharge the battery.

I am 5’8” and the bike fits just fine. My husband is 6’4”. He can still ride it but it’s certainly not the most comfortable – much taller than that and you’re likely to hit the handle bar with your knees.

Pro’s:
-Compact enough to fit into a small trunk
-Easy Set up
-3 Pedal assist modes (Mode 1 Full, Mode 2 Partial, Mode 3 Next to nothing)
-Built in headlight, taillight, and horn
-Taillight flashes when braking – even if the lights are turned off
-Comfortable, wide seat
-Rear suspension works great
-Comes with 2 keys and electric functions will not work without the key in place and turned

Con’s:
-Not great for airline travel because the battery is not designed to be removable
-Display shows metric speed and distance only
-A bit heavy
-The manual leaves a lot to be desired – not a lot about the bike BUT its all fairly self-explanatory
text_fidelity_b: Sailnovo Electric Bike, Electric Bicycle with 18.5mph Electric Bikes for Adults Teens E Bike with Pedals, 14" Waterproof Folding Mini Bikes with Dual Disc Brakes

text_fidelity_a: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds I am slow brained at mechanical things and my first Coleman tent I bought a decade ago took way too much time and frustration from my vacation in the great outdoors to figure out and it had too many pieces so I had to keep referencing the manual.  Plus I had to buy a duffle bag to keep it in because no average human could refit it in the case it came in.  Looks like Coleman too was slow brained, but now it's the opposite with this tent.  It really did take just a few minutes my first time setting it up.  I'm sure my second will be 60 seconds or less.  And afterward I was able to fit it in the carrying case, though I wish it were just a little bigger because I needed help squishing the sides together when zipping...like me now at size 14 trying to get into my wedding dress of 30 years ago.  I'm so glad I can put the tent up by myself.  I use an extra long cot from Walmart and had to set it on the diagonal to fit and even then it's poking the tent fabric a little on the outside.  There isn't much room left on either side of the cot's interior.  I'll keep this tent, but I wish I bought the tent for six people, even though I often camp alone.  I like having space to set a little desk and walk around.  I haven't been in rain yet, but I did spray the outside with water repellant.  I looked all around at the seams and didn't see the seam irregularities some here complained about.  It looks really pro.  In the middle of the day I went inside to take a nap on a day that was about 80-85 degrees.  It was pretty warm even with all the windows unzipped.  The sun was beating down directly overhead, so I'm ordering the rain top even though it doesn't rain much in So CA.  I'm thinking and hoping that maybe that rain top will deflect some of the heat from direct sunlight.  If you too are slow brained, I'd strongly suggest watching some online videos like on YouTube to see how people set up this tent before you begin.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds

text_fidelity_a: Hunting: Edge By Expedite H2o Quiver Magnet There is a little lever that rotates over the batteries, so they don't fall out. therefore batteries falling out is not an issue. I cut a small piece of  Remington camo cloth for the top of the lids to knock off the glare and place two or three of these among 6 decoys in several spots around the blind.  They give lots of movement to the decoys and they really draw the ducks on calm days.  Battery life is not very good, so you will need to change them daily if you spend more than four or five hours in the blind and I find that if I replace the batteries at the end of the hunt if needed it just takes a moment to set them out for the next hunt. Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries 6.4 oz #10 Can I bought this intending to keep it as part of my emergency supplies but ended up using it when I was laid up at home sick and didn't have the energy to go grocery shopping.

In terms of taste, they're fine with a nice tartness. Mostly I put them in my oatmeal, but I like them just as well straight out of the can. But I have to pace myself or else I'd plough through half in one sitting. Whether rehydrating them according to the directions provided or tossing them into a recipe where they'll draw moisture from other ingredients, these plump up well and taste good. The size of the slices is just right for my purposes, though it would be easy to reduce them to bits or powder before rehydrating if you wanted to.

Other reviewers have already explained why no one should be shocked at the amount of product you receive versus the size of the can it's sent in, so I won't repeat that here and will only note that I got the amount I expected and paid for. While I get that using one size of can is probably the most cost effective and efficient way for Augason, I do wish this came in a smaller container, partly because I want to take advantage of my limited storage space.

For me, the packaging is the only negative to this, though it's not a dealbreaker. I've already ordered another can to replace the one I'm using now.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries 6.4 oz #10 Can

Greeshow Green Water filter Element for GS-2801 Green Water Filter, Pre-Filter Replacement Element, Easy to Replace Very light (less than a pound), great for backpacking, and certainly useful in emergencies when no clean water is available. The device comes in a well-designed pouch, with space for the hose, filter, and pre-filter. The pouch has a carabiner that can be easily attached to your backpack, if you are hiking. Includes a light that is useful if you are filtering water at night.

Claims to remove 99.9999% impurities, though I have no way to test this myself.

The instruction manual has some information missing. In English, it does not state the maximum life of the filter. In Japanese, it seems to say it is 1000 liters. The Amazon page information states information that seems contradictory. On the one hand, it states that the water filter has a lifespan of 30,000 liters (that information is reinforced by two illustrations). On the other hand, it says that the filter element needs to be replaced after 1,000 liters. Perhaps the pre-filter element needs to be replaced after 1,000 liters, while the main filter in the device itself lasts for 30,000 liters? The translation from Japanese does not seem to be completely accurate. I checked the Amazon page for the filter + pre-filter replacement, and it states they last for 30,000 liters. The inconsistency is a bit concerning.

text_fidelity_a:
Carrom 510.01 Balance Board [[VIDEOID:cdea6a4f11cba6bceb8d6b8b83d8a0a6]] This is an awesome balance board! I bought it in 2004, and it has held up really well for the past 9 years. Amazon was out of stock for a couple of years, so I'm super glad that it's back in stock, so I can recommend it to my friends.

This board is different than other balance boards that I've used, and I really liked that. Even if you have another balance board, I'd recommend this one, too. It's probably most similar to skateboarding or snowboarding, but it will help your balance in any sport. It took me about three weeks to get to the point that I am today, but I started out super uncoordinated. You'll probably pick it up much faster. I thought it was a great balance board to learn on, too. I definitely felt a sense of accomplishment after I got my balance enough to stay up on it for a minute or two.

It says the weight limit is 300 lbs, but this is super sturdy. I think it would actually work anywhere up to a 400 pound person.

It's pretty simple. You just roll back and forth and balance on top of it. If you got really good at it, you could do tricks and turns, but I'm not good enough to do much more than roll back and forth. I feel like it's really good exercise, too, and you could use weights on it, too, if you got to be really good at it.

Pros:
+Works on any surface. I've used it mostly on carpet.
+Extremely sturdy. It would be very hard to break this.
+Helps you prepare your balance for any sport or activity
+Low impact, so you can use this even if you have sore joints
+After you get used to it, you could watch TV, play video games, or read a book while you're balancing

Cons:
-Very simple. You just roll back and forth.
text_fidelity_b: Carrom 510.01 Balance Board
